subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static truck model without joints, built from boxes, roughly 7m long, 2.6m wide, and 3m tall, facing +Z, with six wheels across three axles.

I'm sketching the layout: cab up front, cargo bed with container or missile launcher at the rear, a roof turret, neon trim, and decal textures like emblems, hazard stripes, and camo, pulling panel and metal textures from the clockwork kit plus a glow kit. I'm working out wheel positions along three axles and a gunmetal color scheme accented with neon cyan, magenta, and amber.

Writing helper functions for boxes and parts...

Still placing wheel and armor parts...

For the cab, I'm considering a sloped hood box and thinking about whether to loft stations along the body or extrude a side profile instead, working out the cross-section direction for the extrusion.

I settle on extruding a side-view polygon tracing the bumper, hood slope, windshield, and roof outline, keeping the cab around 3.5 units tall with 2.4 width, planning to add a metal panel color and a tilted glowing windshield plane along the slope.

Still computing side window geometry...

Still writing windshield geometry...

Now I'm planning the roof details—light bar with glowing amber/magenta boxes, antennas, sensor dome, and a turret with twin barrels—plus front-end elements like a bumper wedge, grille slits, glowing headlight strips, bull bar, winch, angled armor plates, and a possible skull emblem decal on the door.

I'm adding a "UNIT 2077" decal, hood vents, and twin exhaust stacks behind the cab with glowing tops, then working out the cargo bed geometry and the rotation math for an angled missile launcher pod mounted on the deck.

Still working out tube placement...

Now I'm thinking about rear details: side ammo boxes with glow stripes, tail lights, rear ramp, bumper, tow hooks, maybe a small roof drone pad, keeping the design functional but not overloaded.

Adding a tiny quad drone on the bed behind the launcher, plus a radar dish on a tilted mast at the rear left. I'm also considering cyan neon underglow strips beneath the chassis, weighing whether to add visible fuel tanks on the chassis rails but deciding they'd conflict with the wheels or just be hidden under the deck, so I'll skip those and cable bundles too, maybe adding some armor spikes for the cyberpunk feel instead.

Now I'm planning antennas, a glowing neon sign panel reading "2077" and "ARC-7 / CORP SEC" on a side panel, and sketching out the texture set: an emblem with a hex shield and skull-like eye motif, hazard stripes, a HUD windshield texture, side text, grille, and launcher label. For paints I'm using a riveted panelled metal for the hull and a dark teal-black camo countershade for the cab, then adding decals onto the boxes.

Door emblems get placed as textured planes mirrored on both sides of the cab, oriented outward so text reads correctly from either side, with the neon sign glowing while other emblem parts stay unglowed. I'm sinking the wheel cylinders slightly into the ground to fix clearance against the flat-bottomed geometry.

Now I'm building helper functions for boxes and cylinders, then constructing the wheel assembly: a tire cylinder, a metal hub, a glowing cyan ring made from a torus oriented along the wheel axis, and five lug bolts arranged in a circle around the hub face.

Deciding to go with 72 lug parts total, placing small boxes around each tire's radius with rotation to simulate tread lugs.

Wheels do poke outside the cab a bit, so I'll add fender arch boxes over each wheel to cover that, plus a front bumper with glow strips, slit-style glowing grille boxes on the front face, and small glowing headlight boxes.

Now adding a roof lightbar in alternating magenta/amber, plus a roof-mounted turret with a cylindrical base, a head block, two forward-facing barrel rods, and a glowing cyan sensor sphere as its eye.

Adding rear cab antennas with glowing tips, exhaust stacks behind the cab with orange-glowing tips, and framing the cargo bed deck with side rail walls.

Now I'm designing the missile launcher cradle with support legs, a pivoting base, and a 3x2 grid of tubes housing red-tipped warhead cones, plus hazard stripe decals on the pod top.

For the rear of the vehicle, I'm adding magenta tail lights, a bumper, and a ramp light, then placing a tilted radar dish on the cab roof using a lathed bowl shape to avoid colliding with the launcher.

Now I'm planning side details: tool lockers on the skirts with glowing cyan strips, plus a thin underglow box running along the chassis between the wheels for extra detail.

Next I'm sketching cab elements: door panel lines and handles, side mirrors with a glowing screen, a sloped roof armor plate, and small hazard vents angled along the tilted hood surface.

For texture work, I'm planning two modest SVGs: a hexagonal shield emblem with cyan outlines and "77" lettering with chevrons, plus a simple side text graphic.

Then I'm sketching the HUD panel with a dark gradient background, cyan scanlines, and a triangle accent, alongside hazard stripe and grille slit textures.

Now I'm double-checking the API imports before writing the final build code -- glow, panelled, metal, patches, stripes, and countershade modules -- then starting the cab extrusion geometry.

Working through the cab's coordinate placement, bumper bounds, and lug details, then planning decal planes for door emblems and side rail text positioned along the bed skirt.

There's a risk of mirrored text, but I'll set that aside for now and just go ahead and write it out.
